sources.title: Prosperity: Product Sparsity Based Design for Efficient Spiking Neural Network Acceleration

anchors.supports: PyTorch runtime activations; lossless/iso-accuracy; SystemVerilog PPU, spiking-neuron array and SFU; 8-bit weights; commercial 28-nm DC; CACTI 7.0 buffers; DRAMsim3 off-chip power; cycle-accurate simulator.

VGG-16/CIFAR100 at 500 MHz/28 nm: Prosperity 0.529 mm2, 390.10 GOP/s, 299.80 GOP/J, 737.17 GOP/s/mm2; 13.27x throughput versus Eyeriss. Eyeriss/Stellar use 168 PEs versus Prosperity/PTB/SATO/MINT 128. PTB/SATO/MINT transformer comparisons cover linear layers because they do not handle attention/layer normalization; Stellar uses paper statistics because its modification is unavailable.

Accelerator-model comparisons report 14.2x Eyeriss, 7.4x PTB, 4.8x SATO, 3.6x MINT and 2.1x Stellar; simulated-ASIC versus measured A100 comparison is explicitly end-to-end for spiking transformers and averages 1.79x performance and 193x energy efficiency; same-architecture ablation averages 3.2x over bit sparsity, up to 7.4x.
Reported total area is 0.529 mm2 and power is 915 mW for the plotted Spikformer/CIFAR10 case; DRAM appears in power breakdown and TCAM detector is the largest on-chip power component.
The repository identifies a cycle-accurate simulator and baseline implementations; the Figure 8 workflow reports end-to-end runtime and energy for the included paper workloads.
Power/area reproduction is excluded because the Synopsys scripts are unavailable; CACTI buffer area and DRAM power are separately modeled in the released evaluation flow.

sources.title: Phi: Leveraging Pattern-based Hierarchical Sparsity for High-Efficiency Spiking Neural Networks

anchors.supports: Simulator consumes model activations and calibrated patterns; Preprocessor, L1/L2 Processor and Spiking Neuron Array are SystemVerilog/DC in commercial 28 nm; CACTI 7.0 models on-chip buffers and DRAMsim3 off-chip power. VGG16/CIFAR100 at 500 MHz/28 nm: Phi 0.662 mm2, 242.80 GOP/s, 285.81 GOP/J and 366.70 GOP/s/mm2, or 26.70x throughput versus dense Eyeriss.

Across evaluated model/dataset cases, Phi reports performance gains of 12.18x PTB, 6.57x SATO, 6.29x SpinalFlow and 3.45x Stellar; energy-efficiency gains are 31.59x Eyeriss, 13.48x PTB, 2.77x SATO, 2.23x SpinalFlow and 4.93x Stellar. Energy evaluation includes core, buffer and DRAM contributions.

On-chip area/power breakdown totals 0.662 mm2/346.6 mW; PAFT adds 1.26x performance and 1.1x energy efficiency; Phi without PAFT is lossless versus bit sparsity, while PAFT has a minor accuracy decrease. Compression approximately halves activation traffic and PWP prefetch reduces the unprefetched weight-traffic penalty.
Average 4.5x over bit sparsity and 38x over dense are explicitly theoretical computation speedups, not measured or simulated accelerator speedups.

sources.code_availability_boundary: No official Phi simulator repository was identified from the paper/DOI and author-facing links inspected on 2026-08-24. This is a bounded search result, not a claim that no repository exists. Any local Phi-like adapter must be labeled clean-room, not official Phi.

shared_limits: Both works use a cycle/performance simulator plus 28-nm DC and CACTI/DRAMsim3 models; neither paper reports fabricated-silicon or post-layout signoff evidence for the quoted accelerator results.
Both define an SNN operation around sparse accumulation/addition, so GOP/s must not be compared to MAC-based accelerators without an explicit operation convention.
On-chip area excludes off-chip DRAM area; energy may include modeled DRAM accesses. Logic power, SRAM power and DRAM energy must be kept as separate ledger rows.
